newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER ON TUESDAY.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar ended Tuesday's interbank market weaker on the key U.S. dollar, on the back of continued import pressure with little support forthcoming from the central Reserve Bank, dealers said.
"It looks like the market is still very short and the central bank doesn't seem to be doing anything. We opened with a 10-point spread but the spreads have now become wider," one dealer said.

Dealers said the local dollar's free fall which began last Wednesday when a large import payment left the market some Z$80 million short, was intensified on Friday by Reserve Bank governor Leonard Tsumba's statements published in a local paper that the unit was overvalued against the U.S. dollar.
He hinted that the bank would allow it to depreciate further in order to maintain export competivemess.
"It's now up to the central bank to intervene heavily and stabilise the currency," one dealer said on Tuesday.
The Zimbabwe dollar finished the day at 11.5500/7500 on the U.S. dollar from 11.5200/6500 late Monday but was firmer against sterling at 18.7600/19.1100 compared to 18.9320/9690.
It was at 6.3100/4200 from 6.2440/2565 against the mark and at 2.5200/5600 against South Africa's rand from 2.5200/5275.
